maria: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression on rtx-a100-32 when autotune switched short-seq flows to the new fused-attn kernel. Profiling attached below.

maria: perf summary (p50 tokens/sec):
```
old (sticky-path): 12.8k tokens/s
new (autotuned fused): 9.4k tokens/s  <-- 26% drop
launch overhead measured +1.8ms per request on short seqs (<=64)
KV cache hit-rate unchanged
```

maria: hypothesis: fused kernel has higher launch/setup cost but wins at long seqs; scheduler started routing short seqs to it after autotune stats aggregated. Continuous batching + small bursts amplify launch penalty.

devon: ack. Can you paste the exact router decision trace for a few hits? I want to see seqlen distribution vs chosen kernel.

maria: sure, grabbing one trace:
```
[trace id=ak-742] request1 seq=24 -> kernel=fused-attn (path=fused_fast)
 request2 seq=32 -> kernel=fused-attn
 request3 seq=8  -> kernel=fused-attn
 batching window 5ms, batch size 3, launch for fused 1.9ms
```

kai: interesting — scheduler's autotune score function currently uses avg tokens/s over last 5m and doesn't penalize per-request launch cost. so high throughput at long seqs skews the pick.

ash: could be KV cache interplay too: fused path allocates a slightly different KV layout so warmup cost for cold keys is higher — but maria said KV hit-rate unchanged so maybe not primary.

ben: quick mitigation: add a seqlen-based bias back into the score (e.g., penalty = launch_ms / (seqlen_mean * tokens_per_step)). That way short sequences avoid high-launch kernels.

maria: +1. Also thinking we should cap autotune weight changes during rollout windows (hysteresis). yesterday's change moved 85% of short flows in one minute.

perf-bot: automatic regression alert created: RG-210305-01. Attached flamegraphs and bucketed p50/p90 by seqlen.

devon: plan: (1) revert the autotune update for hw-profile rtx-a100-32 (quick rollback flag), (2) add seqlen-penalty to scoring, (3) run an A/B test with synthetic short-seq traffic. Any objections?

kai: No objections. For (2) we should compute launch_ms per-kernel per-hw and persist a moving median, not avg, to avoid noise. Also include continuous-batching window size in the penalty: penalty = launch_ms * min(1, batching_window_ms / expected_batch_build_ms).

ash: for (3) I can spin up the A/B using existing load harness. We'll run 1 hour and compare p50/p90 and token-cost.

maria: I'll post a quick rollback flag:
```json
{"route":"short-flow", "autotune_override":"sticky-path", "expires":"2103055234"}
```

ben: after rollback, let's also run a short bisect to find the autotune change commit that created the new scoring behavior. suspect CL 5487 (autotune: add global token-weighting).

devon: note — rollout policy allowed the autotune change to apply cluster-wide because 3/3 safety checks passed; we should add seqlen-coverage check to rollout gate.

ops-bot: deploy rollback accepted by infra (ticket INF-9123). Canary rollback to 10% of nodes in region us-west2 started.

maria: early canary numbers after rollback (10min):
```
canary p50 short-seq tokens/s -> 12.6k (back to baseline)
canary p90 -> 14.9k
cpu/gpu utilization unchanged
```

kai: good sign. Follow-ups: store per-kernel launch_ms histograms, add seqlen-aware gating in autotuner, and add a continuous-batching sensitivity test in the perf suite (vary batching window 1..10ms). I'll file tickets.

maria: filing: TKT-210305-a (seqlen-penalty in autotune), TKT-210305-b (launch_ms histograms), TKT-210305-c (batching sensitivity tests). Assigning to kai/ash/ben.

ben: for postmortem note — this is a classic throughput-vs-latency tradeoff: autotune optimized for avg throughput across mixed workloads and lost the short-tail latency/launch cost. We should document expected kernels' regime (short/long/hybrid) in model catalog so autotune has priors.

maria: agreed. Also adding model-catalog fields: preferred_seqlen_range and launch_cost_estimate_ms.

devon: thanks everyone. I'll keep the thread updated with bisect results. If anyone sees anomalies after the 100% rollback, ping in #eng-runtime. :thumbsup:

ash: launching the A/B now (traffic synthetic). reporting in 40m.

perf-bot: scheduled perf run: AB-210305-1 running.

maria: thanks — closing the alert if canary stays healthy after full rollback.
